title: Baptism
definition: Baptism is the visible ordinance of water that identifies a believer with Jesus Christ in His death, burial, and resurrection.
summary: Baptism is the visible ordinance of water that identifies a believer with Jesus Christ in His death, burial, and resurrection.
christFocus: Jesus commanded baptism and was Himself baptized, and baptism points to union with Him, cleansing by grace, and new life through His saving work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Baptism is a public sign of belonging to Christ. It does not replace faith in the Gospel, but it visibly declares that the believer is identified with Jesus and His saving work.

Scripture connects baptism with death to the old life and new life in Christ. The water points beyond itself to the cleansing, union, and resurrection life that salvation brings through Jesus.

Baptism also connects believers to the visible community of faith. The baptized person is not merely making a private statement; they are being marked as one who belongs to Christ and His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers need a visible reminder that their old life does not define them. Baptism declares that Christ’s death and resurrection are now the story that names them.

This doctrine also protects baptism from becoming empty ritual or spiritual achievement. Its power is not in performance but in the Savior to whom it points.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Remember baptism as a call to live openly for Christ. If you have not been baptized as a believer, seek faithful pastoral guidance. If you have, let its meaning encourage you to walk in newness of life by the Spirit.
